title: Word Ladder II
description:
A **transformation sequence** from word `beginWord` to word `endWord` using a dictionary `wordList` is a sequence of words `beginWord -> s_1 -> s_2 -> ... -> s_k` such that:

- Every adjacent pair of words differs by **exactly one character**.
- Every `s_i` for `1 <= i <= k` is in `wordList`. Note that `beginWord` does not need to be in `wordList`.
- `s_k == endWord`.

Given two words `beginWord` and `endWord`, and a dictionary `wordList`, return **all the shortest transformation sequences** from `beginWord` to `endWord`, or an empty list `[]` if no such sequence exists. Each sequence should be returned as a list of the words `[beginWord, s_1, s_2, ..., s_k]`.

You may return the sequences in **any order**, though the words within each sequence must appear in exact transformation order.
constraints: beginWord, endWord, and wordList[i] consist of lowercase English letters.
All the words in wordList are unique.
The sum of all shortest transformation sequences does not exceed 10^5.
hints: Run a level-by-level BFS starting from `beginWord` to discover the shortest distance to every reachable word, stopping as soon as the level containing `endWord` finishes.
Do not mark a word as visited until the entire current BFS level has been expanded — otherwise you would miss alternative shortest paths that converge on the same word at the same depth.
Record each word's predecessor list (parents from the previous BFS level) to form a shortest-path DAG, then backtrack from `endWord` to `beginWord` so dead-end branches are never explored.

examples.explanation: There are 2 shortest transformation sequences of length 5: "hit" -> "hot" -> "dot" -> "dog" -> "cog" and "hit" -> "hot" -> "lot" -> "log" -> "cog".
The endWord "cog" is not in wordList, so no valid transformation sequence exists.
"a" differs from "c" by one character and "c" is in wordList, so ["a", "c"] is the unique shortest sequence.
